title: Is Life Basically Pointless? Solomon's Hot Take
paragraphs: Yo, so these are the thoughts of the 'Quester,' who was King David's son and the king in Jerusalem.

He—the Quester—basically said, 'Everything is smoke. Just a puff of smoke.' For real, he felt like everything was pointless. Like, what do you even get from all the hard work you put in your whole life? You grind and grind, and for what?

One generation is out, the next one is in, but the world just keeps on spinning. Nothing really changes. The sun comes up, the sun goes down, and then it just does it all over again. The wind blows south, then north, just swirling around and around, doing its thing. All the rivers flow into the ocean, but the ocean never gets full. The water just goes back to where it started and flows again. Honestly, it's all kinda boring. Super repetitive. You can't really find any deep meaning in it. It's boring to watch and boring to listen to. Whatever has happened before is gonna happen again. There's legit nothing new in this world. It's the same old story, year after year. If someone's like, 'Yo, check this new thing out!'—don't even get excited. It's probably been done before. Nobody remembers what happened in the past, and nobody in the future will remember what we're doing now. Don't expect to leave a legacy or whatever.

So yeah, you can call me the Quester. I was the king of Israel in Jerusalem, and I made it my mission to figure everything out. I looked into everything that happens on this planet. And let me tell you, it's not all that great. God made life pretty tough, honestly. I've seen it all, and it's like trying to catch smoke or chase the wind.
Life is like a twisted-up rope you can't straighten out, or a math problem that just doesn't add up.

I told myself, 'Look, I'm smarter and wiser than any king who was in Jerusalem before me. I've got all this wisdom and knowledge.' But in the end, I realized that even chasing wisdom and knowledge is just as pointless. It's all just chasing the wind.
The more you know, the more problems you have. The more you understand, the more it hurts.

title: My Epic Search for Meaning (and Fun)
paragraphs: I was like, "Alright, let's just go all out and have some fun. Let's see what pleasure is all about." But honestly, it was all for nothing. Just a bunch of smoke.

My take on the whole "fun" lifestyle? Insane! Inane! Just pointless. And trying to be happy all the time? Who even needs that? I tried to figure out how absurd life is with some wine and all the brainpower I had. I really wanted to find something useful for us to do in the short time we have on this planet.

And man, I did some epic stuff. I built huge houses, planted vineyards, and designed these awesome gardens and parks with all kinds of fruit trees. I even made pools to water all the trees. I bought a bunch of slaves, and they had kids, so I got even more slaves. I had more cows and sheep than anyone in Jerusalem before me. I stacked up so much silver and gold, stuff I got from kings and kingdoms. I had a whole choir to sing for me, and the best part? A bunch of gorgeous girls.

I was seriously ballin'. I was way more successful than anyone who came before me in Jerusalem. And the crazy thing is, I kept a clear head through it all. I got everything I wanted; I never told myself no. I just went for it, whatever I felt like doing. I squeezed every last drop of fun out of every single thing I did. That was my reward for all my hard work.

But then I took a good, hard look at everything I had done, all the sweat and effort I put in. And you know what I saw? Nothing but smoke. It was like trying to catch the wind. There was no point to any of it. Seriously, nothing.

Then I started thinking about what it means to be smart versus being dumb. I mean, what can you even do after you've been a king? It's a tough act to follow. You just do what you can, and that's it. But I did realize that being smart is better than being dumb, just like light is better than darkness. But in the end, it doesn't even matter. The smart people know where they're going, and the dumb people are just stumbling around in the dark, but they all end up in the same place. We all have the same fate.

When I realized that I have the same fate as a fool, I had to ask myself, "Then what's the point of being so wise?" It's all just smoke, man. Nothing but smoke. The smart and the dumb both just disappear. In a day or two, everyone forgets about them. Yep, the smart and the dumb both die. That's it.
I hate life. From what I can see, everything that happens on this earth is just a bad deal. It's all smoke and trying to catch the wind.

And I hated everything I had worked for and collected on this earth. I can't take any of it with me. I have to leave it all to whoever comes after me. And who knows if they'll be worthy or worthless? They'll just take over everything I worked so hard for. It's all smoke.

That's when I just gave up. I gave up on hoping for anything on this earth. What's the point of working so hard if you just have to give everything to someone who didn't even try? It's all smoke. A bad deal from start to finish. So what do you really get from a life of hard work? Just pain and sadness all day long. You can't even get a good night's sleep. It's all just smoke.

The best thing you can do is just have a good time and do your best to get by. That's how I see it. It's all up to God. Whether we eat or not, it's all in His hands. God might give wisdom, knowledge, and joy to the people He likes, but sinners are stuck with a life of hard work, and in the end, they just have to give everything they earned to the people God likes. It's all just smoke and trying to catch the wind.

title: There's a Time for Everything
paragraphs: Basically, there's a right time for everything, a specific season for every single thing on earth:

A time to be born and a time to die,
A time to plant and a time to pull up what you planted,
A time to kill and a time to heal,
A time to tear down and a time to build up,
A time to cry and a time to laugh,
A time to be sad and a time to dance,
A time to be close and a time to hold back,
A time to hug and a time to not hug,
A time to search and a time to give up,
A time to hold on and a time to let go,
A time to tear and a time to mend,
A time to be quiet and a time to speak up,
A time to love and a time to hate,
A time for war and a time for peace.

So, what do people really get from all their hard work? I've seen the grind God has given us. He has made everything beautiful in its time. But he's left us in the dark; we can never really know what God is up to, from start to finish. I know that there is nothing better for people than to be happy and to do good while they live. That everyone should eat and drink and find satisfaction in all their work—this is a gift from God.
I know that everything God does will last forever; you can't add to it or take anything from it. God does it so that people will revere him.
What was, is. What will be, is. That's just how it always is with God.

And I saw something else under the sun: In the place of judgment—wickedness was there, in the place of righteousness—wickedness was there. I said to myself, “God will bring into judgment both the righteous and the wicked, for there will be a time for every activity, a time for every deed.” I also said to myself, “As for humans, God tests them so that they may see that they are like the animals.”

For real, the fate of humans and the fate of animals is the same. As one dies, so dies the other. They all have the same breath; humans have no advantage over animals. It's all meaningless, like smoke. All go to the same place; all come from dust, and to dust all return. Who knows if the human spirit goes upward and if the spirit of the animal goes down into the earth? So I saw that there is nothing better for a person than to enjoy their work, because that is their lot. For who can bring them to see what will happen after them?

title: Why Going Solo is a Total Fail
paragraphs: So then I looked at all the messed-up, unjust stuff that happens in the world. I saw victims crying their eyes out with no one to comfort them, and the people with power just crushing them, with no one to step in and help. It made me think the dead are better off than the living who are still dealing with all this. But honestly, the luckiest person is the one who was never even born, who never had to see all the garbage that goes down on earth.
Then I noticed how much of people's hard work and ambition is just because they're jealous of someone else. What a total waste. It's like trying to catch smoke. Or spitting into the wind.
The fool just kicks back and does nothing, but that laziness is basically a slow-motion way to ruin your life.
It's way better to have one handful of stuff and be chill, than two fistfuls and be stressed out all the time. That's just more chasing smoke.

Then I turned my head and saw yet another wisp of smoke: this one person, totally alone—no kids, no family, no friends—yet working obsessively late into the night, always greedy for more and more, never even stopping to ask, "Why am I working like a dog and never having any fun? And who even cares?" More smoke. A really bad deal.

Honestly, having a buddy is way better than rolling solo. You can share the work and share the rewards. If one of you falls, the other is there to help you up. But if you're alone and you fall, you're in big trouble.
Plus, two people sleeping in one bed keeps you warm. If you're alone, you'll just be shivering all night.
By yourself, you're an easy target. With a friend, you can stand up to anything. And if you can get a third person? A squad of three is basically unbreakable.

A poor but wise kid is way better off than an old, foolish king who has no clue what's going on. I saw a kid just like that who started with nothing, went from rags to riches, and everyone was hyped for him to be the new king. But even with all that, the excitement didn't last. People got bored and lost interest. See? It's all just smoke. Totally pointless, like spitting into the wind.

title: Don't Just Talk, Live It
paragraphs: Yo, when you go to God's house, be real. Go there to actually listen and learn. That's way better than just going through the motions with some sacrifice, which honestly just makes things worse.

Don't just run your mouth or say stuff without thinking. And for real, don't be too quick to tell God stuff just because you think it's what he wants to hear. He's the one in charge, not you. So, less talk, more listening. It's that simple.
Overwork messes up your sleep, and overtalk just makes you look like a fool.

When you make a promise to God, keep it—now. No excuses. God isn't impressed by empty words. If you say you're gonna do something, do it. It's way better to not make a promise in the first place than to make one and then flake.
Don't let your words get you into deep trouble. When you're held accountable, you can't just be like, "Oops, my bad, didn't mean it." Why would you want to make God mad and have him come after you?
But for real, when all the fake stuff, daydreams, and empty chatter fade away, you've still got this solid truth: Respect God.

And don't get too bent out of shape when you see poor people getting treated like trash, and justice being a total joke everywhere. It's like a pyramid of corruption, from the low-level guys all the way to the top. It's a messed-up system, and you can't really do anything about it. But hey, at least the earth is real and provides for everyone—even a shady king gets food from the fields.
The one who's all about money never has enough of it. The one who's obsessed with getting rich is never satisfied with the profit. It's all just chasing smoke.
If you're all about money, you'll never have enough. If you're obsessed with being rich, you'll never be satisfied. It's all just chasing smoke.
Putting in a good, honest day's work means you'll sleep like a baby, whether you had a fancy dinner or just some ramen. But a rich person with a full stomach just lies awake stressing.

I've seen some seriously bad luck go down: a guy saves up a ton of money, way more than he needs, and then loses it all in some sketchy business deal. He has a kid but has nothing to give him. He came into the world with nothing, and he'll leave with nothing. That's some tough luck, for real. He came with nothing, he leaves with nothing. So what was the point of working so hard for a paycheck that just disappears like smoke? Just to live a miserable life in the dark?

So, after checking out how things work on this planet, I've figured out the best way to live: take care of yourself, have some fun, and do your best at whatever job you've got for as long as God lets you live. That's pretty much it. That's what we get. Yeah, we should totally enjoy what God gives us, both the good stuff and the ability to actually enjoy it. Just accept what you're given and find joy in your work. It's a gift from God! God gives us joy in the here and now. It's pointless to sit around worrying about how long you're gonna live.

title: Rich & Miserable? What's the Point?
paragraphs: I've been taking a good, hard look at how things are, and let me tell you, it's pretty messed up. And you can tell people are feeling it.

For example, there are these people God totally blesses with everything—money, property, a killer reputation—basically everything they've ever dreamed of. But then, God doesn't even let them enjoy any of it. Some random person swoops in and gets to have all the fun with their stuff. It's just... pointless. A total ripoff.

Like, imagine someone has a ton of kids and lives a super long life but never actually enjoys it—even if they get a huge funeral at the end. Honestly, I think a baby that was never born is better off. It comes into the world and leaves without a name, never seeing or knowing anything, but it's still in a better spot than anyone who's alive.
Even if you lived for a thousand years—or even two thousand!—what's the point if you never actually enjoyed your life? Don't we all just end up in the same place anyway?
We're always grinding to feed our own desires, but our souls are left feeling empty.

So, what advantage does a wise person really have over a fool, or over some poor person who's just scraping by? The best you can do is grab what you can, while you can. Don't just sit around assuming something better will show up later. It's all just smoke in the end. Totally pointless, like spitting into the wind.
Whatever's gonna happen, happens. Your destiny is already set. You can't argue with fate.

The more words get spoken, the more smoke fills the air. And who's better off for it? Who even knows what's best for us in this short, fleeting life we live? And who can possibly tell us what's going to happen next?

title: Real Talk: Wisdom vs. Hype
paragraphs: Having a good rep is way better than being loaded. Your last day says more about you than your first.
You'll have more 'aha' moments at a funeral than at a party. I mean, that's everyone's final destination, right? You might actually learn something real there.
It's actually better to cry it out than to laugh it off. Sure, your face gets all puffy, but it's like a deep clean for your soul.
Wise people aren't afraid to deal with the tough stuff, like pain and sadness. But fools? They just waste their time on pointless fun.
A straight call-out from a wise person is worth way more than the noise and hype of fools.
The laughter of fools is super shallow, like the sound of twigs burning up fast. It's all just smoke, no real substance.
Being cruel can make even the smartest person dumb, and it can break even the strongest spirit.
Endings are honestly better than beginnings. Sticking with something is more impressive than just starting it.
Don't lose your cool so fast. Getting angry always comes back to bite you. You can spot a fool by the lumps on his head—his own anger put them there.
Don't be that person always saying, 'Man, things were so much better back in the day.' That's not a wise question to ask.

Wisdom is even better when you've got some money to go with it, especially if you get both while you're young. It's like double protection: wisdom and wealth! Plus, wisdom gives you this extra energy.
Just look at what God has made. Who could possibly straighten out all the crazy, beautiful curves and angles of His creation?
When life's good, enjoy it. When it's bad, take a look at yourself. God gives us both good and bad days so we don't take anything for granted.

I've seen it all in my short, kinda weird life—I've seen good people die young, and I've seen terrible people live super long lives. So don't burn yourself out trying to be perfect, and don't get a big head thinking you're so wise. Trust me, it won't get you anywhere. But don't go wild being bad, either. And don't be reckless. Why die for no reason?
It's best to see both sides of things. Someone who respects God deals with all of reality, not just the parts they like.
One wise person with wisdom is stronger than ten powerful leaders in a city.
There's not a single person on earth who is 100% good, who is totally pure and never messes up.
Wisdom gives one wise person more strength than ten strong men give their city.

I really tried to get wise, I put everything into it. I wanted to be wise, but it was just out of my reach, like, way out there and super deep. Does anyone ever really figure it out? I went all in, studying and trying to find the meaning of life. I also wanted to understand what evil, stupidity, and craziness were all about.

Here's something I, the Quester, figured out: a woman can be a real trap, full of schemes to get you. If you're lucky, you'll get away from her; but if you're not paying attention, you'll get caught. At least, that's what I've seen while I've been trying to make sense of everything. But I still haven't found the wisdom I was looking for. I couldn't find one man or woman in a thousand who was worth it. But I did see one good thing: God made us all good and straight, but we're the ones who have made a huge mess of things.

title: Life's Not Fair, But Here's the Hack
paragraphs: Honestly, being wise is the best. Like, actually getting the point of life? It just makes your eyes sparkle and you're way chiller in how you talk and act.

Look, just do what the leader says. You made a sacred promise to obey, so don't start stressing and second-guessing when things get tough or annoying. You're there to serve his pleasure, not yours. The boss has the final say, and you can't just be like, 'Yo, what are you even doing?' Following orders isn't gonna kill you; the wise person obeys promptly and gets it right. There's a right time and a right way for everything, even if we mess it up most of the time. And for real, nobody knows what's coming next. Who's gonna tell us?
You can't control the wind or trap it. You don't get to decide when you die. You can't just pause a war mid-battle. And if you do messed-up stuff, that same energy isn't gonna save you.
I saw all this while I was trying to make sense of the world. As long as people have the power to hurt each other, it's just gonna be like this.

I once saw these seriously bad dudes get a fancy funeral on sacred ground. Then everyone went back to town and said all this super nice stuff about them—in the exact same place where those guys did all their dirt! It's all just a bunch of nonsense, for real.
Because people who do bad things don't get their karma right away, everyone else starts to think they can get away with anything.

Even when someone messes up a hundred times and lives a long life getting away with it, I'm still sure that the best life is for people who respect God and live like they know He's watching. The person who does wrong won't have a truly 'good' life. No matter how long they live, their days will be empty and pointless, like a shadow—all because they don't respect God.

Here’s something that happens all the time that is totally wild: Good people get the punishment that bad people deserve, and bad people get the rewards that good people deserve. I'm telling you, it makes zero sense. Total nonsense.

So, I'm all for just enjoying life. The best thing we can do on this earth is to eat, drink, and have a good time. That's our reward for all the hard work we have to do in the short time God gives us here.

When I decided to go all-in on wisdom and really look at everything happening on earth, I realized that even if you stayed up 24/7 and never blinked, you'd still never figure out what God's plan is. You can search as hard as you want, but you won't get it. No matter how smart you are, you'll never understand the full story.

title: Life's Crazy, So Just Live It
paragraphs: Alright, so I've been thinking about all this stuff, like, really digging deep. And here's what I figured out: good people, wise people, everything they do is basically in God's hands. But honestly, whether they're dealing with love or hate, they have no clue what's coming next.

It's pretty wild, right? It's one fate for everybody—the good, the bad, the righteous, the wicked, the nice, the mean, church people and people who skip church, the committed and the uncommitted. I find this outrageous—the worst thing about living on this earth is that everyone's lumped together in one fate. No wonder so many people are obsessed with evil and go off the rails. Life just leads to death. The end.

But hey, if you're still breathing, you've got a shot. Like they say, 'a live dog is better than a dead lion.' At least when you're alive, you know you're gonna die. The dead? They know nothing, get nothing. They're just... gone. Nobody even remembers them. All their crushes, their beefs, their dreams—poof, vanished. They've left zero mark on the world.

So, for real, just live your life! Eat your food like it's the best thing ever, drink your drink with a happy heart. God's actually cool with you having a good time. Dress up every day. Go all out with colors and cool accessories. Enjoy life with the person you love, every single day of this crazy ride. Each day is a gift from God, and it's all you get for the grind of being alive. So make every day count! Whatever comes your way, just go for it, 100%. This is your one and only shot, 'cause in the grave—where you're definitely headed—there's no work, no thoughts, nothing.

I was walking around the other day and had this realization about how things are on Earth— the fastest runner doesn't always win, the strongest fighter doesn't always come out on top, the smartest person isn't always happy, the cleverest person isn't always rich, and the most talented person doesn't always get the praise. Sooner or later, we all get hit with bad luck.
You can't see trouble coming. It's like fish getting caught in a net or birds in a trap. People get snagged by random, bad stuff all the time.

One time, I was watching how wisdom plays out in the real world, and I saw something that really made me think. There was this tiny town with hardly anyone in it. A powerful king attacked it, setting up all his gear to take it over. But there was this poor but super-wise guy in the town who saved everyone with his wisdom. And you know what happened? He was totally forgotten right after. (I guess 'cause he was just some poor dude.)
But still, I'm telling you, being wise is way better than being strong, even if that poor wise guy got ignored and forgotten.
The quiet advice of a wise person is way more powerful than the shouting of some fool in charge.
Wisdom is better than weapons, but one hothead can mess everything up for everyone.

title: Big Brain Moves vs. Epic Fails
paragraphs: You know how a single dead fly can make a whole bottle of fancy perfume smell nasty? Well, it's the same with a little bit of foolishness—it can totally wreck a ton of wisdom.
Being wise points you in the right direction, but being stupid leads you down the wrong path. It's that simple.
Even when a fool is just walking down the road, they have no clue where they're going. The way they walk just screams, "Hey, look, it's that fool again!"
If your boss gets mad at you, don't just quit. Staying calm can actually chill them out and fix the situation.

Here’s something messed up I’ve seen in the world, a mistake that’s on the people in charge: they give immaturity a place of prominence, handing important jobs to clueless people, while the smart, experienced ones get pushed to the side. I’ve seen newbies living the high life, while the veterans who know what they're doing are basically ignored.
Be careful: the trap you set for someone else might be the one you get caught in. And watch out, because the person you're scheming with might just turn on you.
Safety first: quarrying stones is dangerous. Be alert: felling trees is risky. Always be alert.
Remember this: if your ax is dull, you're gonna have to work way harder. It's better to use your brain so you don't have to use as much muscle.
If a snake bites you before the snake charmer can do their thing, what's the point of calling them afterward? It's too late.
When a wise person talks, it's always smooth and helpful. But when a fool talks, they just end up destroying themselves. They start by saying something dumb and finish by spewing crazy, evil stuff.
Fools talk way, way too much, just blabbering on about things they know nothing about.
A hard day's work leaves a fool so exhausted that they can't even figure out how to get back home.

It's bad news for a country when its king is like a clueless kid and its leaders party all night. But it's awesome for a country when its king is mature, and the leaders are responsible and don't just get wasted all the time.
If you're lazy, your house is gonna fall apart. A lazy person's roof is always gonna leak.
Life's about having fun with friends (laughter and bread) and enjoying the good times (wine), but let's be real—money is what makes everything happen.

Don't talk trash about your leaders, not even in your head. And don't say bad things about powerful people, even when you're alone in your room. Somehow, that kind of talk always gets out. It's like little birds hear your gossip and spread it everywhere.

title: YOLO, But Make It Smart
paragraphs: Go ahead, be generous with what you have—it's like a spiritual investment that pays off big time, for real.
Don't be a hoarder; share your stuff and be a blessing to people. This could be your last night.

When the clouds are full, it's gonna rain. When a tree falls, that's where it lies. Stop overthinking and waiting for the perfect conditions. Just do the work. Stop staring at the sky and get on with your life.
Think about it—you can't fully explain the miracle of a baby forming in the womb, right? In the same way, you're not gonna understand every single thing God is doing. It's a mystery, and that's okay.
Get up and get to work in the morning, and stay on your grind until the evening. Don't just watch the clock. You never know which effort will be the one that leads to success in the end.

Man, waking up to a new day is honestly the best feeling. It's awesome to be alive. Even if you live a super long life, don't take a single day for granted. Soak up every good moment, because tough days will come too. And honestly, most of the stuff that happens is temporary, like smoke.

To all the young people out there: make the most of your youth. Enjoy your energy. Follow your heart's passions. If something seems right, go for it. But just remember, there are still rules. You're accountable to God for everything you do.
So live freely and enjoy life—you're not young forever. Youth disappears as fast as a puff of smoke.

title: Remember Your Creator Before It's Too Late
paragraphs: Yo, make sure you honor, enjoy, and remember your Creator while you're still young, before the tough years hit and you start losing your energy. Before your eyesight gets blurry, the world looks fuzzy, and you're stuck inside by the fire during the cold winters.

When you get old, your body isn't on your side anymore. Your muscles get weak, your grip loosens, and your joints get all stiff. It's like the curtains are drawn on the world. You can't just go wherever you want, whenever you want. Everything just kind of stops. The normal sounds of the house disappear. You get woken up by birds chirping. Mountain hikes are a thing of the past. Even just walking down the street can feel terrifying. Your hair turns white like apple blossoms, adorning a super fragile, matchstick-thin body. Yeah, you're on your way to your forever home, and your friends are already starting to plan your funeral.

Life is beautiful, but it's over in a flash. The precious and amazing life we have ends. Our bodies go back to the ground they came from, and our spirits go back to God who gave them to us in the first place.
It's all smoke, just smoke. the Quester says everything's smoke.

Besides being wise himself, the Quester also taught other people what he knew. He carefully considered, studied, and put together a ton of proverbs. The Quester tried his best to find the perfect words to write down the simple truth.
The words of the wise push us to live a good life. They're like nails hammered in tight, holding our lives together. They come from God, the one Shepherd who guides us.

But hey, my friend, when it comes to anything more than this, just chill. People will never stop publishing books, and studying all the time will just wear you out until you're useless. So, here's the final, most important thing:
Respect God and do what he tells you.
And that's it. Eventually, God is going to bring everything we've ever done out into the light and judge it all based on what our secret intentions were, whether they were good or bad.
